title: Phased opt-in bridge and migration kit for streaming & toolcall structured-output changes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Short: Provide an opt-in compatibility bridge and a migration toolkit for clients affected by upcoming structured-output and streaming/tool-call API changes. Deliverables include a behavior-flag timeline, client SDK shims, a proxy adapter for legacy streaming+toolcall clients, migration guides, and backward-compatibility test harnesses.

Why: Recent runtime changes to structured output schemas and streaming semantics (chunking, close semantics, and toolcall tokenization) improve correctness and performance but risk breaking existing clients. We need a low-friction path to adoption while protecting production apps.
background: Runtime teams will release structured-output schema v2 which enforces typed envelopes and stricter chunk boundaries for streaming. This change breaks callers that relied on loose parsing of partial fragments.
Tool/function calling will introduce a canonical tokenization for tool invocation boundaries; older clients may mis-interpret partial toolcall tokens during streaming.
Past deprecation rollouts caused customer-incidents when clients upgraded unexpectedly; the goal is to avoid that with guarded opt-ins and observable canaries.
goals: Provide a behavior-flagged opt-in path so existing customers can migrate on their schedule.
Ship client SDK shims and a lightweight proxy adapter that can translate legacy client streams to v2 semantics in-flight.
Create migration guides, test suites, and a replayable compatibility harness to validate client behavior pre- and post-migration.
Define a clear deprecation schedule with automated telemetry gates for stage promotions.
success_criteria: Behavior flag implemented server-side and exposed in SDKs and docs.
Proxy adapter PoC available and validated against 10 representative customer streams.
Migration guide published with cookbook examples for Node/Python/Go SDKs.
Backward-compatibility test harness (replayer + fuzz corpus) passes against both legacy and v2 runtime modes.
Canary rollout executed with zero-severity customer regressions in two pilot accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Server opt-in flag (compat.mode=legacy->v2) with default=false and audits logged.
SDKs include 'compatibilityBridge' option and a migration helper CLI.
Proxy adapter documented and Docker image published to internal registry.
Migration guide includes sample prompts, expected deltas, and a checklist for customers.
Automated tests added to CI to run the replayer corpus on every PR that touches streaming/toolcall paths.
tasks: Design API for behavior flag and config (PM + ENG spec)
Implement server-side behavior flag and telemetry hooks (ENG)
Build SDK migration helpers for Node/Python/Go (DevEx)
Prototype proxy adapter and run integration tests with replayer (ENG)
Author migration guide and cookbook (PM + Docs)
Prepare canary rollout plan and contact pilot customers (Customer Success)
Add compatibility replayer to CI and create fuzz corpus (QA + Research)
Measure and publish performance delta between v1 and v2 in docs (Benchmarks)
risks: Proxy translation may add latency or edge cases that mask real client bugs.
Customers with custom parsers might depend on subtle invalid behaviors.
Telemetry gates may not surface low-volume regressions; need manual review.
SDK adoption lag could cause confusion if flags are only server-side.
notes: Consider a 'shadow-run' mode where both legacy and v2 payloads are emitted to diagnostics for a period.
Discuss baked-in fallback: if replayer detects >x% failures, automatically keep customer pinned to legacy for 30d.
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure behavior flags are configurable in private control plane.
